subject: YEAR-TO-YYYY function
notes: cite.py --check 15.100.4 'The equivalent arithmetic expression is as follows' OK (rule 2); --check 15.100.4 'In the year 1995, the returned value for FUNCTION YEAR-TO-YYYY (4, 23) is 2004' OK (NOTE 1, anchored under 2) a)). READ CobolDate.cs lines 128-130: 'return max % 100 >= yy ? yy + 100 * (max / 100) : yy + 100 * (max / 100 - 1);' - arm a is 'argument-1 + 100 * (FUNCTION INTEGER (maximum-year/100))' guarded by 'FUNCTION MOD (maximum-year, 100) >= argument-1', arm b subtracts 1, both transcribed exactly. THE OPERATOR EQUIVALENCE IS EARNED, NOT ASSUMED: FUNCTION MOD is a true modulo and FUNCTION INTEGER is a FLOOR, which differ from C# '%' and '/' only for a negative dividend - and r6 (enforced two lines above) guarantees maximum-year >= 1700 > 0, so on every path that reaches this expression the two agree. The result is therefore always >= 1601, which is what makes the errored-path 0 an unambiguous sentinel for the delegating wrappers (lines 153/172). BOTH ARMS ARE TESTED against hand-derived values: conformance:cases/15.23.4-Returned-value-rule/intrinsics_date_window T1 (r2a, 2004) and T2 (r2b, 1898) are the spec's own NOTE-1 pair, T3/T4 straddle the r2a/r2b boundary at the same maximum-year 2049 (49 => 2049, 50 => 1950), T5 pins argument-1 = 0 under r2a; unit:CobolDateWindowingTests.YearToYyyy_SpecNote1_Examples re-pins the NOTE-1 pair at the runtime API. NOTE 2 is informative (a sliding vs fixed window description) and describes the implemented behavior: argument-3 omitted reads the execution-time clock (sliding), a written argument-2 + argument-3 fixes the ending year. REFUTED: REFUTED: verdict UPHELD at CONFORMS - I tried to break the operator-equivalence argument and it holds. cite.py --check 15.100.4 'The equivalent arithmetic expression is as follows' -> OK §15.100.4 2). Both arms re-read at CobolDate.cs lines 128-130 and matched against the rendered spec text at specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 34090-34106: arm a is guarded by 'FUNCTION MOD (maximum-year, 100) >= argument-1' and arm b subtracts 1, transcribed exactly. I RE-DERIVED THE EQUIVALENCE RATHER THAN ACCEPTING IT: C# '%' and '/' agree with FUNCTION MOD (true modulo) and FUNCTION INTEGER (floor) only for a non-negative dividend, and r6 - enforced two lines above at line 126 - guarantees maximum-year >= 1700, so every path that reaches this expression has a positive dividend. I also re-derived the result range the delegating wrappers depend on: arm a yields [1700, 9999]; arm b fires only when MOD(max,100) < argument-1, so at the minimum max = 1700 it requires argument-1 >= 1 and yields 1600 + argument-1 in [1601, 1699]. The floor is 1601, never 1600, so the errored-path 0 really is an unambiguous sentinel for lines 153 and 172. Both arms are pinned to hand-derived spec values by conformance:cases/15.23.4-Returned-value-rule/intrinsics_date_window (T1/T2 = the §15.100.4 NOTE-1 pair; T3/T4 straddle the arm boundary at maximum-year 2049) and re-pinned at the runtime API by CobolDateWindowingTests.YearToYyyy_SpecNote1_Examples, whose values I checked against NOTE 1 myself. A third direct YEAR-TO-YYYY arm-b line exists that the record did not cite: pb65_date_windowing.cob line 20 'FUNCTION YEAR-TO-YYYY(50, 10, 1900)' pinned YY-A3=1850. CAVEAT, deliberately NOT a downgrade: like every rule here, this expression is unreachable on the float carrier's one- and two-argument references (see AR-15.100.3-5). Unlike r6 and RV-15.100.4-1 - whose text is about the RESOLVED ARGUMENT VALUES, which that carrier corrupts - this rule is a pure function of maximum-year and argument-1 and is completely and correctly implemented wherever it executes. Downgrading it too would count one defect three times and misreport a finished transcription as partial.
